== Ars Technica article and Merchandise (Oct 2026) ==
* '''Build notes:''' Eric Berger's Ars Technica article (5 Dec 2015) is about the 1997 Worlds, not 2015 Worlds, so it is cited here and not on [[2015 World Championship]]. All 13 article images saved to Wayback 13 Oct 2026; article copy is the 9 Oct 2026 capture. Finalist shirt photos (front, back, sleeve) were provided by Bill Bisco; they do not appear in the article.
* '''Missing data:''' Berger's 1997 Worlds finish ("near the bottom" of about 64) is not a number, so his place is blank. Tom Hoge (2015 home game) has no page; no tournament record found.
* '''Possibly faulty data:''' the article calls the embroidered item a "swag bag"; the photo shows only the embroidery and a zipper.

== Qualifier pages (October 2026) ==
=== Build notes ===
* Qualifier list and event pages built from Decipher's "1997 Regionals and Open Events" page (Wayback 3 May 1999) plus the June 1997 NewsFlash reports (Calamari I, Coruscant II, Dagobah I, Tatooine I).
=== Possibly faulty data ===
* Dagobah: the finalist list gives Atlanta (Dragon Con, 29 June) = Chris Vickers and Mobile (MobiCon, 30 May) = Shelby Abercrombie. The NewsFlash report on the MobiCon qualifier says Vickers won it, beating Stephen Lanza. The Mobile page follows the report; the Atlanta row is left without a winner and has no page.
* Denver (31 May): the list names Thaddeus Chenoweth; the NewsFlash report says Joshua Andersen beat Chenoweth 2–0 in the final. The page follows the report.
* Sydney: the list spells the winner "Brett Chaiyawatt"; the NewsFlash report spells "Chaiyawat" twice. Page uses Chaiyawat.
* Origins Open (18 July): Decipher lists Rick Sollman as champion; forum t=8037 (fan compilation) gives Origins 1997 1st Clint Hays, 2nd T.J. Holman. Page follows Decipher.
* DragonCon Open (27 June): the list prints its city as "Columbus, Ohio" (the Origins city); DragonCon is in Atlanta. City left out of the page.
* Spellings in the list: "Yannick LaPointe", "Phillipp Jacobs", "Jeremy LaMere".
=== Missing data ===
* Environment (legal sets) for each qualifier is not stated in the source, so the Format cells are blank.
* Kiffex (Edinburgh, 16 August) and Sullust (Milan, 13 September) are the existing pages [[1997 Kiffex Regionals]] and [[1997 Sullust Regionals]]; their "Dates" lines (August / October 1997) were not changed. Sullust's existing date comes from the Deck Designs label "10/97" and differs from the list's 13 September. [[User:Datacard Grok|Datacard Grok]] ([[User talk:Datacard Grok|talk]]) 21:45, 13 October 2026 (UTC)

== Style pass (2026-10-15) ==
=== Possibly faulty data ===
* Field size: Wikipedia's Round 1 count is 52 (kept); Eric Berger (Ars Technica, 2015) remembered "about 64 competitors and six Day 1 games". The Decipher qualifier list gives 51 qualifiers plus 2 invitees (53).
* 1997 Dagobah Regionals (Atlanta), 29 June 1997: the table has two rows, one with a blank winner and one with Chris Vickers, previously annotated "(per Decipher list; disputed)". The dispute is not documented on the page; Vickers also won the 30 May Mobile Dagobah Regional.
* Final twelve: Trandosite spells "Enriue Pascal"; matched to [[Enrique Pascual]] (1997 Ithor Regionals (Barcelona) winner) under the small-world rule.
=== Missing data ===
* The forum post (p1300392) gives Michael Krause 10th; his Results row still has a blank place.
=== Marginal cuts ===
* Caption: "World Championship Finalist embroidery from the 1997 prize, photographed in 2015." Source: Eric Berger, Ars Technica (5 December 2015).
* Caption: T-shirt back text began "A Moment of Triumph …".
* "The constructed pool was Premiere - Cloud City." (duplicate of the Format section).

== Day 1 / Day 2 rewrite (2026-10-23) ==
=== Build notes ===
* Rewrote to Format, Qualifiers, Day 1, Day 2 from Decipher's 97worldfinals site (Wayback). Saturday cut: semifinalists.html. Sunday finishes: gameresults2.html. Championship scores: scoreboard.html. Schedule: report1.html. 53 invited / 52 played: index.html plus satsummary.html (Gamble missed). Hotel photo is Commons File:MarriottNorfolk.jpeg (CC0, PghPhxNfk, 10 January 2016), uploaded as File:Norfolk Marriott Waterside.jpg.
* Wikipedia Round 1 52 dropped from Format. Decipher 53 invited / 52 played is the body figure.
* Krause 10th, Palmer 4th, Pascual 6th, Winkelhaus 7th, Zetsche 8th, Chenoweth 9th, Lapointe 11th filled from the Sunday table.
=== Possibly faulty data ===
* Shirt back prints Dec. 6-7 1997 (play days). Decipher billed 5–7 December including Friday arrival.
* Championship: Trandosite summarized Jacobs's 23-Force Dark win as too much for Riboulet's manipulator to catch. Decipher scoreboard has Riboulet winning Game 2 Dark 2(11); combined Jacobs 2(+12).
* report1 spells "Tom Litsche" and "Kendrick Summer's chair"; dest as [[Tom Lischke]] and [[Kendrick Summers]].
* Saturday "all 53 champions play" is the pre-event schedule on report1; satsummary records Gamble missed and 52 played.
* Berger remembered about 64 competitors and six Day 1 games. Official Saturday is eight games among 52.
* Feldman PDS2 names Beggar and Sack with Obi-Wan and Revolution; Results keep Imperial Holotable / Obi-Wan's Hut from the deck pages.
* Denver: Chenoweth made Saturday 3rd / Sunday 9th. Qualifiers table still follows the NewsFlash (Andersen beat Chenoweth).
* Atlanta/Mobile: both [[Chris Vickers]] and [[Shelby Abercrombie]] are on Decipher's 53 and in Sunday sealed (Vickers 11th, Abercrombie 28th).
=== Missing data ===
* No magazine recap found (InQuest #33–#36, Duelist #23, Insider 36–38).
* Saturday individual pairings (gameresults.html) not archived.
* Event photos (photospage1.html) not archived. Decipher player portraits (phillippjacobs.jpg, paulfeldman.jpg, michaelriboulet.jpg) are not in the Wayback Machine.
* Berger's constructed place is still blank.

== First Anthology sealed article (2026-10-23) ==
=== Build notes ===
* Moved the sealed consolation below Results and split it to [[1997 Decipher World Championship First Anthology Sealed]]. Decipher Report 10 (sealedsummary.html) is the standings source. report1 bills 9 a.m.–3 p.m. Sunday "Star Wars CCG First Anthology Sealed Deck tournament for non-semifinalists."
* Minted [[First Anthology Sealed]] and added it to [[Formats]] Limited / sealed. No 1997 sealed rulesheet found. Card pool is the First Anthology box. The 1997 event ran four preliminary games, then a final of the top two (Kessenich vs McCann).
=== Possibly faulty data ===
* Place 38 Jeremy Virgil printed "02 (-31)" on sealedsummary; dested as 2 (-31).
* Decipher "filled with cards from all of the Star Wars CCG expansions to date": First Anthology (May 1997) listed contents are Premiere, A New Hope, Hoth, Jedi Pack, and Special Edition previews. Dagobah (April 1997) is not in that box list. Cloud City (November 1997) is after the product.
=== Missing data ===
* Deck size and round time for this 1997 event. The June 1999 Decipher tournament guide is later generic sealed procedure and postdates the event.
